records.note: Comment c-1 from Priya Nair, resolved (resolvingUserId/resolvedAt set), body about payment gateway timeout, createdAt 2026-03-03. Satisfies all conditions on a single comment; clean match.

This distinction matters for i-web-5, where the person and topic requirements are each satisfied by a different comment on the same issue — the author's phrasing correctly implies both must hold on the same comment, which matches my reading and correctly excludes i-web-5. Otherwise the author's c1 (resolved) and c3 (date) map directly onto my conditions 3 and 5. The author omits an explicit uniqueness assumption, but that's an unstated background assumption rather than a testable condition, so it doesn't create a real discrepancy."

ambiguity_effects.explain: Linear has a distinct, well-known feature where a comment thread can be explicitly marked 'resolved' (captured here by resolvingUserId/resolvedAt). All issues in this dataset are still in the 'Todo' workflow state, ruling out any confusion with issue-level resolution. A careful reader familiar with Linear would settle on the formal resolved-thread-status reading, and the records confirm this is the intended and only sensible reading here.

Grammatically 'about the payment gateway timeout' sits immediately after 'comment ... from Priya Nair' and naturally describes the comment's content, not the issue's overall topic. Even considering the alternate reading (the issue itself being 'about' payment gateway timeouts), no issue title unambiguously fits that description better than the comment-content reading already selects (i-web-1), so the two readings don't diverge in practice for this record set.

The request never states a year, so in isolation a careful reader can't be fully sure whether 'March 3' means this year or some prior year. In practice every comment in the dataset is dated in 2026, so the ambiguity doesn't change which record is selected — but it is a genuine, unresolved gap in the wording of the request itself.
